# Shareholder Requirements for Private Companies in Nepal

## Maximum Number of Shareholders
A private company in Nepal is limited to a maximum of **fifty shareholders**. This requirement is explicitly stated in the Company Act, which outlines that "the number of shareholders of a private company shall not exceed fifty" [CompanyAct2006.pdf p.10].

## Exclusions from Shareholder Count
It is important to note that employees who purchase shares under a scheme for selling shares to employees are **not counted** as shareholders for the purpose of this maximum limit. The Act specifies that "any employee who has purchased a share of a company under a scheme of selling shares to employees... shall not be counted as a shareholder" [CompanyAct2006.pdf p.10].

## Memorandum of Association
The memorandum of association for a private company must include a statement regarding the maximum number of shareholders allowed, which is required by the Act [CompanyAct2006.pdf p.19].

## Conclusion
In summary, a private company in Nepal can have up to **fifty shareholders**, with specific exclusions for certain employee shareholdings. This structure is crucial for maintaining compliance with the Company Act and understanding the regulatory framework governing private companies in Nepal.
